 Hundreds of Taiping homes hit by flash floods after six hours of rain
 By ANNABELLE LAWRENCE 
 Monday, 16 Nov 2026
 | 7:14 PM MYT

 IPOH: Six hours of continuous heavy rain caused flash floods in several parts of Taiping on Monday (Nov 16), with about 200 houses affected in the worst-hit area of Taman Kim Yong.
 Flooding was also reported in Kampung Sungai Relong in Kamunting, where officials visited affected areas to assess the situation and discuss immediate measures with the relevant agencies.
 State science, technology, innovation and environment committee chairman Teh Kok Lim said the latest floods underscored the need to improve drainage systems and flood mitigation facilities in affected areas.
 Teh, who is also Aulong assemblyman, visited the affected areas with the Taiping parliamentary and state assembly teams, together with officers from the Taiping Municipal Council and Irrigation and Drainage Department.
 “Discussions were also held with technical agencies to identify the causes of the floods and formulate short- and long-term solutions,” he said in a statement.
 Teh said one of the key areas of focus was a 500m-long flood bund previously built at a cost of RM200,000.
 He said the bund had played an important role in preventing floodwaters from spilling into nearby residential areas.
 Following discussions with the department, several immediate measures were identified, including placing sandbags to control rising water levels and using large soil-filled bags to construct temporary barriers.
 Other measures include repairing water-control valves and clearing temporary retention ponds and related facilities to ensure water can flow smoothly.
 Teh said longer-term flood mitigation projects would also be given priority.
 “Solutions must take into account the terrain, direction of water flow and capacity of the drainage system to address the root causes of flooding, rather than merely carrying out repair works after every incident,” he said.
 He said continuous follow-up efforts by the Taiping parliamentary and state assembly teams over the past four years had resulted in several flood mitigation projects aimed at improving drainage in affected areas.
 These included the construction of a main drain in the town area, river drainage works in Taman Berjaya, Kamunting, and the first phase of a flood mitigation project in Taman Kim Yong.
 Teh said the teams would continue working with the council, department and other agencies to improve drainage and flood mitigation infrastructure and safeguard the safety and well-being of Taiping residents.
